findings.title: Avoid starting import promises that have no rejection handler
findings.body: Every import() starts when this module is evaluated, but consumers await only the entries they need. If an unused app's chunk fails to load or its module throws during initialization, that promise has no rejection handler. The failure becomes an unhandled rejection and can terminate the Node process, even when the current request never uses that app. Export loader callbacks and invoke the selected loader so its failure propagates to an awaiting caller, or explicitly handle every eagerly started import.

findings.title: Await the newly asynchronous reschedule callbacks
findings.body: forEach discards the promises returned by its newly async callback. Consequently, a rejection from getCalendar—including a CalendarService constructor failure that the surrounding try/catch previously caught—now becomes an unhandled rejection instead of being logged. Reschedule also proceeds to emails and can return true before calendar loading and deletion finish. Await Promise.all over a map, or use an awaited for...of loop. The same conversion in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and bookingsRouter.requestReschedule needs the same treatment.
